page: Vultr voc-g-24c-96gb-480s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided by a 480 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present in this configuration.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing the processor in the top 10% of tested hardware. Multi-core CPU performance is also strong, ranking in the top 25%. Memory sub-system performance is robust, highlighted by a strong PassMark memory score in the top 25%, though raw memory read and write bandwidth benchmarks fall within the average range. In specialized workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier performance for text generation using small language models, alongside strong image processing capabilities. Other operations, including database transactions, static web serving, and standard software compilation, perform at average levels.

Given its dedicated AMD EPYC cores and balanced 1:4 memory-to-vCPU ratio, this instance offers high resource density and reliable performance without the virtualization overhead of shared-core models. The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage makes it a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring consistent compute power and fast local disk access. It is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, medium-scale web serving, image processing pipelines, and lightweight machine learning inference tasks.
